# divizu

> A deterministic DSL → SVG compiler for architecture diagrams that coding agents can write.

divizu lets an agent express a repository's wiring as a layered drawing. Roots
sit at the bottom, dependencies above them, and shared providers are drawn once
with a cable to each consumer. The renderer has zero runtime dependencies, needs
no browser, and produces deterministic output for the same DSL.

## Start here

- Agent skill: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/skills/divizu.md
- Playground: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/playground.html
- Reference manual: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/docs.html
- Quickstart source: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/examples/quickstart.di
- Shared layers: https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/examples/shared.di
- Large system map (28 blocks): https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/examples/large.di

## Use it

Ask the agent:

> Use divizu to diagram this project's architecture. Read
> https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/skills/divizu.md and follow it. Write the
> architecture as a `.di` file, validate it, render it to SVG, and show me the
> result.

Fastest delivery without installing anything: URL-encode the DSL and return a
playground link.

```text
https://jeysef.github.io/divizu/playground.html#dsl=<encodeURIComponent(dsl)>
```

To render a file:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Jeysef/divizu
cd divizu
npm install
npm run build
node dist/cli.js architecture.di --check
node dist/cli.js architecture.di -o architecture.svg
```

## Roles

Exactly four:

- `root` — program/entry point; cannot be used as a provider.
- `component` — internal code that gets wired in.
- `boundary` — database, network, queue, filesystem or vendor adapter.
- `value` — config/injected data with no behaviour.

Language details go in `tag:`. `provides:` declares service keys. Shared
providers are drawn once; `<- fresh Provider` opts into a separate instance.
`src: "path:line"` records provenance for `--check --verify-src`.

## DSL

```dsl
root CheckoutApp "cmd/api" {
  src: "cmd/api/main.go:24"
  needs Orders <- OrdersLive
  needs Clock
}

component OrdersLive "order use case" {
  provides: Orders
  src: "internal/orders/live.go:18"
  tag: service
  needs Db <- DbLive
  needs Logger <- LoggerLive
  modules: ValidateCart, PriceOrder
}

boundary DbLive "postgres" {
  provides: Db
  src: "internal/db/pg.go:12"
  tag: closer
}

value AppConfig "config" {
  provides: Config
  src: "internal/config/config.go:9"
}
```

```dsl
file       = { block } ;
block      = role ident [ string ] "{" { NL | directive } "}" ;
role       = "root" | "component" | "boundary" | "value" ;
directive  =
    "provides"   ":" list
  | "needs"      key [ "<-" [ "fresh" ] ident ]
  | "modules"    ":" list
  | "candidates" ":" candidate { "," candidate }
  | "tag"        ":" list
  | "src"        ":" string
  | "label"      ":" name ;
list       = name { "," [ NL ] name } ;
candidate  = name [ "(" name ")" ] ;
```

Braces are mandatory. Directives end at a newline or `;`. Comments only start at
a token boundary, so `C#Parser` is a name. Quote names with spaces or
punctuation. Every non-root block must be referenced; every root must be
unreferenced. Cycles are rejected. Use unbound needs for external systems.

## Properties

- Input: plain-text `.di` DSL.
- Output: deterministic, self-contained SVG with a layered DAG layout.
- Runtime: zero dependencies, no DOM, no canvas, no headless browser.
- Validation: file-relative `line:column`, fix hints, `--check --json`,
  `--check --verify-src`.
- License: MIT.
